laws.title: Hands-Free Driving Law
laws.subtitle: AL Code §32-5A-350 — No handheld device while driving
laws.fullDescription: Alabama's hands-free law (2023) prohibits holding or using a handheld mobile device while operating a vehicle. Hands-free Bluetooth or dashboard mounts are required.
laws.penalty: $50 first offense, $100 second, $150 third+. Two points added to driving record.
laws.exceptions: Emergency 911 calls, law enforcement on duty, parked vehicle

quiz.q: What is the fine for a first handheld phone offense in Alabama?
quiz.explanation: First offense is $50 under Alabama's 2023 hands-free law.

laws.title: DUI — Blood Alcohol Limit 0.08%
laws.subtitle: AL Code §32-5A-191 — Impaired driving prohibition
laws.fullDescription: Driving with a BAC of 0.08% or higher is illegal in Alabama. For commercial drivers the limit is 0.04%, and for drivers under 21 the limit is 0.02% (effectively zero tolerance).
laws.penalty: 1st offense: up to 1 year jail, $600–$2,100 fine, 90-day license suspension. Mandatory ignition interlock for repeat offenders.
laws.exceptions: None

quiz.q: Alabama's BAC limit for drivers under age 21?
quiz.explanation: Alabama enforces a 0.02% BAC limit (near-zero tolerance) for drivers under 21.

laws.title: Move Over Law — Emergency Vehicles
laws.subtitle: AL Code §32-5A-58.2 — Lane change for stopped vehicles
laws.fullDescription: Alabama drivers must move over one lane (or slow to 15 mph below the speed limit if lane change isn't safe) when passing any stopped emergency, law enforcement, utility, or tow truck with lights flashing.
laws.penalty: Up to $25 fine and 2 points. Can be enhanced if officer is injured.
laws.exceptions: If lane change is impossible due to traffic or road conditions, reduce speed to 15 mph below posted limit

quiz.q: How many mph below the speed limit must you slow when you can't move over in Alabama?
quiz.explanation: Alabama requires reducing speed to 15 mph below the posted limit when a lane change is not possible.

laws.title: Motorcycle Helmet Law — Under 21
laws.subtitle: AL Code §32-7-7 — Helmet requirement
laws.fullDescription: In Alabama, all motorcycle riders and passengers under age 21 must wear a DOT-approved helmet. Riders 21 and over are strongly encouraged but not legally required to wear helmets.
laws.penalty: $100 fine for minors riding without helmet.
laws.exceptions: Riders 21 and over (no requirement)

quiz.q: At what age is a helmet no longer legally required for motorcyclists in Alabama?
quiz.explanation: Alabama requires helmets for riders under 21; riders 21 and older are not legally required to wear one.

laws.title: Child Car Seat Requirements
laws.subtitle: AL Code §32-5-222 — Child passenger safety
laws.fullDescription: Alabama requires all children under age 6 to be secured in an approved child safety seat or booster seat. Children 6–14 must wear a seat belt. Rear-facing for infants, forward-facing after 2 years/20 lbs, booster until belt fits properly.
laws.penalty: $25 fine per unsecured child. Primary enforcement — officers can stop solely for this violation.
laws.exceptions: Vehicles without seat belts (pre-1967), medical exemptions with physician letter

quiz.q: Up to what age must children be in a car seat or booster in Alabama?
quiz.explanation: Alabama requires a safety seat or booster for children under age 6.

laws.title: Red Light Camera Prohibition
laws.subtitle: Alabama bans municipal red light cameras
laws.fullDescription: Alabama law prohibits the use of automated red-light enforcement cameras by municipalities. Law enforcement must be present to issue traffic citations — no automated ticket systems are allowed.
laws.penalty: Applies to municipalities; automated citations are unenforceable.
laws.exceptions: Toll collection systems, railroad crossing cameras

quiz.q: Are red light cameras legal in Alabama?
options: No, they are prohibited by law
quiz.explanation: Alabama law prohibits automated red-light cameras; human officers must issue citations.

laws.title: Headlights Required in Rain
laws.subtitle: AL Code §32-5-240 — Lights when wipers are in use
laws.fullDescription: Alabama requires headlights to be turned on whenever windshield wipers are in use due to rain, drizzle, fog, snow, or other precipitation. This is a primary offense.
laws.penalty: $100 fine. Primary enforcement.
laws.exceptions: None

quiz.q: In Alabama, when must you turn on your headlights?
quiz.explanation: Alabama requires headlights whenever wipers are in use, regardless of time of day.

laws.title: Implied Consent — Chemical Testing
laws.subtitle: AL Code §32-5-192 — Refusal consequences
laws.fullDescription: Any person driving in Alabama impliedly consents to chemical testing (breath, blood, or urine) for alcohol or drugs if lawfully arrested for DUI. Refusal results in automatic license suspension.
laws.penalty: 1st refusal: 90-day suspension. 2nd refusal within 5 years: 1-year suspension. Refusal can be used as evidence in court.
laws.exceptions: None — refusal still results in suspension

quiz.q: What happens if you refuse a breathalyzer in Alabama after a DUI arrest?
options: Nothing, you have the right to refuse
quiz.explanation: Refusing a chemical test in Alabama triggers an automatic 90-day license suspension under implied consent law.

laws.title: School Bus Stop Arm Law
laws.subtitle: AL Code §32-5A-154 — Must stop for school bus
laws.fullDescription: Alabama drivers on all roadways must stop when a school bus displays its stop arm and flashing red lights. Drivers must remain stopped until the arm is withdrawn and lights stop flashing. Failure to stop is a criminal offense.
laws.penalty: $300–$500 fine, 4 points on license. Possible criminal misdemeanor charge.
laws.exceptions: Divided highway with physical barrier — opposite-direction traffic may proceed

quiz.q: On a divided highway with a physical barrier, must you stop for a school bus in Alabama?
quiz.explanation: On a divided highway with a physical barrier, only same-direction traffic must stop; opposite traffic may proceed.

laws.title: Passing in No-Pass Zones
laws.subtitle: AL Code §32-5A-86 — Prohibited passing
laws.fullDescription: Passing is prohibited in no-pass zones marked by double yellow lines or no-passing signs, within 100 feet of an intersection, railroad crossing, bridge, or tunnel, and when visibility is restricted.
laws.penalty: $100–$300 fine, 3 points added to driving record.
laws.exceptions: Emergency vehicles, passing stopped school bus on divided highway

quiz.q: How close to an intersection is passing prohibited in Alabama?
quiz.explanation: Alabama prohibits passing within 100 feet of an intersection, railroad crossing, bridge, or tunnel.

laws.title: Constitutional Carry — No Permit Required
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-11-73 — Permitless carry enacted 2023
laws.fullDescription: Alabama enacted constitutional carry in January 2023. Adults 21+ who can legally own a firearm may carry a concealed handgun without a permit. Permits remain available voluntarily for reciprocity purposes.
laws.penalty: N/A for permit-less carry (legal). Unlawful carry by prohibited persons: Class C felony.
laws.exceptions: Prohibited persons (felons, domestic abusers), federal restricted locations (schools, post offices, federal buildings)

quiz.q: Since 2023, what age can Alabamans carry a concealed handgun without a permit?
quiz.explanation: Alabama's constitutional carry law (effective Jan 2023) allows adults 21+ to carry concealed without a permit.

laws.title: Stand Your Ground Law
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-3-23 — No duty to retreat
laws.fullDescription: Alabama has a strong Stand Your Ground law. If you are in a place you have a legal right to be, you have no duty to retreat before using deadly force in self-defense, provided you reasonably believe force is necessary to prevent death or serious injury.
laws.penalty: Affirmative defense — if invoked successfully, no criminal liability.
laws.exceptions: Cannot be the initial aggressor, cannot use in commission of a crime

quiz.q: Under Alabama's Stand Your Ground law, is there a duty to retreat?
options: No duty to retreat if lawfully present
quiz.explanation: Alabama's Stand Your Ground law eliminates the duty to retreat anywhere you are legally present.

laws.title: Castle Doctrine — Home Defense
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-3-23 — Presumption of reasonableness
laws.fullDescription: Alabama's Castle Doctrine creates a legal presumption that deadly force is justified when an intruder unlawfully enters your dwelling, vehicle, or occupied business. No duty to retreat applies inside the home.
laws.penalty: Affirmative defense against prosecution.
laws.exceptions: Cannot apply against lawful occupants or co-residents

quiz.q: Does Alabama's Castle Doctrine apply to a vehicle?
options: Only if the vehicle is parked
quiz.explanation: Alabama's Castle Doctrine extends to dwellings, vehicles, and occupied businesses.

laws.title: Prohibited Persons — Firearm Ownership
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-11-76 — Firearms and felons
laws.fullDescription: Alabama prohibits firearm ownership by convicted felons, persons convicted of misdemeanor domestic violence, those under domestic violence restraining orders, fugitives, unlawful drug users, and those adjudicated mentally defective.
laws.penalty: Class C felony for unlawful possession. Up to 10 years in prison for prior felony conviction.
laws.exceptions: None — federal and state law both prohibit possession

quiz.q: Who is prohibited from owning a firearm in Alabama?
options: Convicted felons and domestic abusers among others
quiz.explanation: Alabama (and federal law) prohibits firearm ownership by convicted felons, domestic abusers, drug users, and others.

laws.title: Gun-Free School Zones
laws.subtitle: Federal GFSZA + AL Code — 1,000-foot school zone
laws.fullDescription: Bringing a firearm within 1,000 feet of a school or on school property is a federal crime under the Gun-Free School Zones Act, also enforced in Alabama. Schools may not allow open carry on campus.
laws.penalty: Federal felony: up to 5 years imprisonment. State charges may be additional.
laws.exceptions: Law enforcement, licensed dealers for school programs, permit holders in some states (but Alabama follows federal law)

quiz.q: What is the gun-free zone radius around schools in Alabama?
quiz.explanation: The federal Gun-Free School Zones Act creates a 1,000-foot gun-free zone around schools, enforced in Alabama.

laws.title: Minimum Drinking Age — 21
laws.subtitle: AL Code §28-3A-25 — Underage alcohol prohibition
laws.fullDescription: The legal drinking age in Alabama is 21. It is illegal to purchase, possess, or consume alcohol if under 21. It is also illegal for anyone to furnish alcohol to a person under 21.
laws.penalty: Underage possession: Class C misdemeanor, up to $500 fine. Furnishing to minor: Class A misdemeanor, up to $6,000 fine and 1 year jail.
laws.exceptions: Religious sacramental use, medical use under physician care

quiz.q: What is the legal drinking age in Alabama?
quiz.explanation: The legal drinking age in Alabama, as in all US states, is 21.

laws.title: Open Container in Vehicle — Prohibited
laws.subtitle: AL Code §32-5A-330 — No open containers while driving
laws.fullDescription: It is illegal for drivers or passengers to possess an open container of alcohol in the passenger area of a vehicle on a public highway in Alabama. This applies to any open or unsealed container of alcohol.
laws.penalty: $25 fine for driver. Passenger violation $25. Can elevate DUI suspicion.
laws.exceptions: Passengers in buses, limos, motor homes, or taxis may possess open containers

quiz.q: Can passengers drink alcohol in a moving vehicle in Alabama?
quiz.explanation: Open containers in the passenger area are illegal for both drivers and passengers in Alabama.

laws.title: Dry Counties and Cities
laws.subtitle: AL Code §28-2 — Local option wet/dry elections
laws.fullDescription: Alabama allows individual counties and municipalities to hold elections on whether to permit alcohol sales. Some counties and towns remain completely dry (no alcohol sales). Check local laws before purchasing alcohol, especially in rural areas.
laws.penalty: Selling alcohol in a dry area: criminal charges, license revocation.
laws.exceptions: Private clubs in some dry areas, religious organizations

quiz.q: Can Alabama counties vote to ban alcohol sales entirely?
quiz.explanation: Alabama allows dry/wet elections at the county and municipal level, making some areas completely dry.

laws.title: Sunday Alcohol Sales Restrictions
laws.subtitle: AL Code §28-3-10 — Sunday sales hours
laws.fullDescription: Many Alabama counties and cities restrict Sunday alcohol sales. Restaurants and bars may have different hours than package stores. Some areas require a special Sunday license. Hours typically allowed after 12:00 PM (noon) where permitted.
laws.penalty: Selling outside permitted hours: $1,000 fine, potential license suspension.
laws.exceptions: Wet counties that voted to allow Sunday sales

quiz.q: What is a common Sunday alcohol sales restriction in Alabama?
options: Sales typically only allowed after noon where permitted
Only beer and wine on Sundays
quiz.explanation: In counties where Sunday sales are permitted, sales are commonly restricted to after noon, varying by jurisdiction.

laws.title: Alcohol Sales Hours — Package Stores
laws.subtitle: AL Code §28-3A — ABC store hours
laws.fullDescription: Alabama Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) Board regulates all retail liquor sales. Package stores (selling spirits for off-premises consumption) operate under state-set hours. Sales are prohibited between 2 AM and 7 AM statewide.
laws.penalty: Selling outside hours: license suspension or revocation.
laws.exceptions: On-premises consumption may have slightly different rules by permit type

quiz.q: What are Alabama's statewide alcohol sales blackout hours?
quiz.explanation: Alabama prohibits alcohol sales statewide between 2 AM and 7 AM.

laws.title: Marijuana — Recreational Use Illegal
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-12-213 — Cannabis possession prohibited
laws.fullDescription: Recreational marijuana is illegal in Alabama. Possession of any amount is a misdemeanor for first offense, escalating to a felony for subsequent offenses. Alabama has not legalized recreational cannabis.
laws.penalty: First offense possession (any amount): Class A misdemeanor, up to 1 year jail and $6,000 fine. Second offense: Class D felony.
laws.exceptions: Medical marijuana is legal for qualifying conditions since 2021 with a CANN card

quiz.q: Is recreational marijuana legal in Alabama?
options: No, illegal with jail time possible
quiz.explanation: Recreational marijuana is illegal in Alabama and can result in jail time even for first-time possession.

laws.title: Medical Marijuana — Compassion Act
laws.subtitle: AL Act 2021-450 — Limited medical cannabis
laws.fullDescription: Alabama's Compassion Act (2021) allows medical marijuana for qualifying conditions including cancer, PTSD, chronic pain, and others. Patients must register with the Alabama Medical Cannabis Commission and obtain a CANN card. No smoking allowed — only approved forms (capsules, oils, patches, gummies).
laws.penalty: Using without CANN card remains illegal. No-smoking provision means no cannabis flower.
laws.exceptions: Only registered patients with CANN card; no smoking form permitted

quiz.q: Can Alabama medical marijuana patients smoke cannabis flower?
quiz.explanation: Alabama's medical cannabis law prohibits smoking — only approved forms like capsules, oils, and patches are allowed.

laws.title: Drug Paraphernalia — Illegal to Possess
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-12-260 — Paraphernalia prohibition
laws.fullDescription: Possession of drug paraphernalia (pipes, syringes for drug use, scales, rolling papers when combined with drugs, etc.) is illegal in Alabama. The law defines paraphernalia broadly based on intended use.
laws.penalty: Class A misdemeanor: up to 1 year jail and $6,000 fine.
laws.exceptions: Licensed medical use (insulin syringes for diabetics, etc.)

quiz.q: What is the charge for drug paraphernalia possession in Alabama?
quiz.explanation: Drug paraphernalia possession is a Class A misdemeanor in Alabama, punishable by up to 1 year jail.

laws.title: Alabama Habitual Felony Offender Act
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-5-9 — Enhanced sentencing
laws.fullDescription: Alabama's Habitual Felony Offender Act mandates significantly enhanced sentences for repeat felony offenders. Three prior felony convictions can result in life imprisonment without parole, even for non-violent offenses.
laws.penalty: Life without parole possible for third felony conviction depending on prior offenses' severity.
laws.exceptions: Youthful Offender Act may apply to first-time juvenile offenders

quiz.q: Alabama's Habitual Felony Offender Act can result in what maximum sentence?
quiz.explanation: Alabama's habitual offender law can impose life without parole for repeat felony offenders.

laws.title: Trespassing — Criminal Penalties
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-7-4 — Criminal trespass
laws.fullDescription: Knowingly entering or remaining on property after being told to leave, or on clearly posted property, is criminal trespass in Alabama. Escalates based on circumstances including the nature of the property.
laws.penalty: 1st degree (dwelling): Class A misdemeanor. 2nd degree: Class B misdemeanor. 3rd degree: Class C misdemeanor.
laws.exceptions: Public officials with lawful authority, licensed agents, emergency services

quiz.q: Trespassing on someone's dwelling is which degree of criminal trespass in Alabama?
quiz.explanation: Criminal trespass on a dwelling (home) is 1st degree criminal trespass in Alabama — a Class A misdemeanor.

laws.title: Gambling Laws — Highly Restrictive
laws.subtitle: AL Const. Art. IV §65 — Prohibition on lotteries
laws.fullDescription: Alabama's constitution bans lotteries and has some of the most restrictive gambling laws in the US. Commercial casinos are illegal; no state lottery exists. Dog racing was legal until recently. Charitable bingo is permitted with strict limits.
laws.penalty: Illegal gambling: up to 1 year jail and $6,000 fine. Operating illegal gambling: Class D felony.
laws.exceptions: Charitable bingo with license, social gambling with no house cut in private homes, Native American gaming on tribal land

quiz.q: Does Alabama have a state lottery?
quiz.explanation: Alabama's constitution bans lotteries, making it one of a handful of states without a lottery.

laws.title: Robbery — Degrees and Penalties
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-8-41 — Armed robbery
laws.fullDescription: Robbery in Alabama ranges from 1st degree (armed) to 3rd degree (unarmed). First-degree robbery (using a deadly weapon) is a Class A felony carrying 10 years to life. Robbery is treated very seriously under Alabama law.
laws.penalty: 1st degree: 10 years to life. 2nd degree: 2–20 years. 3rd degree: 2–10 years.
laws.exceptions: None — any taking by force or threat is robbery

quiz.q: What is the minimum sentence for 1st degree robbery (armed) in Alabama?
quiz.explanation: First-degree robbery in Alabama carries a mandatory minimum of 10 years, up to life imprisonment.

laws.title: Computer Crime Act
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-8-102 — Unauthorized computer access
laws.fullDescription: Alabama's Computer Crime Act prohibits unauthorized access to computer systems, networks, or data. Includes hacking, identity theft, computer fraud, and unauthorized modification or destruction of data.
laws.penalty: Ranges from Class C misdemeanor (minor unauthorized access) to Class B felony (fraud over $2,500 or critical infrastructure).
laws.exceptions: Authorized security testing, lawful access

quiz.q: Is unauthorized computer access a crime in Alabama?
options: Yes, ranges from misdemeanor to felony
quiz.explanation: Alabama's Computer Crime Act creates criminal liability ranging from misdemeanor to felony for unauthorized computer access.

laws.title: Fleeing Law Enforcement
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-10-52 — Attempting to elude police
laws.fullDescription: It is a felony in Alabama to intentionally flee from a law enforcement officer who signals you to stop, whether on foot or in a vehicle. Causing injury while fleeing elevates the charge further.
laws.penalty: Base offense: Class C felony (1–10 years). If injury or death results: Class A or B felony.
laws.exceptions: None if you knowingly flee after being signaled to stop

quiz.q: Fleeing from police in Alabama is what type of offense?
quiz.explanation: Intentionally fleeing police is a Class C felony in Alabama, elevating if injury or death results.

laws.title: Bear Wrestling — Prohibited
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-12-5 — Prohibited animal activities
laws.fullDescription: Alabama specifically prohibits bear wrestling exhibitions, bear baiting, and any contest involving a bear. This unusual law was passed to protect bears from cruelty. Participation, promotion, or attendance at a bear wrestling event is illegal.
laws.penalty: Class B misdemeanor: up to 6 months jail and $3,000 fine.
laws.exceptions: None

quiz.q: Is bear wrestling illegal in Alabama?
options: Yes, both wrestling and baiting bears are prohibited
Only if the bear is injured
quiz.explanation: Alabama specifically outlaws bear wrestling and baiting — participation, promotion, and attendance are all illegal.

laws.title: Utility Theft — Illegal
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-8-23 — Theft of utilities
laws.fullDescription: Stealing electricity, gas, water, cable TV, or other utilities by bypassing meters, tampering with equipment, or using service without paying is criminal theft in Alabama.
laws.penalty: Based on value: under $500 = Class A misdemeanor; $500–$2,500 = Class D felony; over $2,500 = Class C felony.
laws.exceptions: Authorized meter testing, emergency service restoration

quiz.q: Stealing $600 worth of electricity in Alabama is what offense?
quiz.explanation: Utility theft between $500–$2,500 is a Class D felony in Alabama.

laws.title: Right-to-Work State
laws.subtitle: AL Code §25-7-30 — Union membership not required
laws.fullDescription: Alabama is a right-to-work state. Workers cannot be required to join a union or pay union dues as a condition of employment. Employers and employees have the right to negotiate individually without union interference.
laws.penalty: Employers who require union membership as condition of employment may face injunctions and damages.
laws.exceptions: Federal employees, railroad and airline workers (covered by federal Railway Labor Act)

quiz.q: In Alabama, can an employer require workers to join a union?
options: No, Alabama is a right-to-work state
quiz.explanation: Alabama is a right-to-work state; employees cannot be compelled to join a union as a condition of employment.

laws.title: Minimum Wage — Federal Rate Applies
laws.subtitle: AL follows federal $7.25/hr minimum wage
laws.fullDescription: Alabama has no state minimum wage law. The federal minimum wage of $7.25 per hour applies. Alabama has not passed any legislation to increase the minimum wage above the federal floor.
laws.penalty: Employers paying below federal minimum wage face federal FLSA enforcement, back pay, and penalties.
laws.exceptions: Tipped employees may receive a lower direct wage if tips bring total to $7.25/hr

quiz.q: What is the minimum wage in Alabama?
quiz.explanation: Alabama has no state minimum wage, so the federal rate of $7.25/hour applies.

laws.title: At-Will Employment
laws.subtitle: Alabama default employment doctrine
laws.fullDescription: Alabama is an at-will employment state. Employers can terminate employees for any reason (or no reason) without notice, and employees can quit for any reason. Exceptions exist for discriminatory termination and breach of contract.
laws.penalty: Wrongful termination in violation of public policy or contract may result in civil liability.
laws.exceptions: Employment contracts, collective bargaining agreements, discrimination based on protected class (illegal)

quiz.q: In Alabama, can an employer fire an employee without giving a reason?
quiz.explanation: Alabama is an at-will employment state; employers can generally terminate for any or no reason, with exceptions.

laws.title: Sales Tax Rate — 4% State + Local
laws.subtitle: AL Code §40-23-2 — State sales and use tax
laws.fullDescription: Alabama's state sales tax is 4%. Counties and municipalities add their own sales taxes, making the combined rate typically 8–10% in cities. Alabama is notable for taxing groceries at the full rate, though reforms have reduced the grocery tax.
laws.penalty: Failure to collect/remit sales tax: interest and penalties, potential criminal charges for willful evasion.
laws.exceptions: Prescription drugs exempt; groceries taxed at reduced 3% state rate (effective 2023)

quiz.q: What is Alabama's state sales tax rate?
quiz.explanation: Alabama's base state sales tax is 4%, with local taxes adding up to 4–6% more in most areas.

laws.title: Business License Required
laws.subtitle: AL Code §40-12-40 — Municipal business license
laws.fullDescription: All businesses operating in Alabama must obtain an appropriate business license from the state and/or municipality. Penalties for operating without a license can include fines and business closure.
laws.penalty: Operating without license: $100–$500 fine per day, injunction to cease operations.
laws.exceptions: Some small sole proprietors selling homemade goods at markets may have lighter requirements

quiz.q: Is a business license required to operate in Alabama?
quiz.explanation: All businesses operating in Alabama must obtain appropriate state and/or local business licenses.

laws.title: Littering — 'Don't Mess with Alabama'
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-7-29 — Litter Control Law
laws.fullDescription: Alabama has aggressive anti-litter enforcement. Throwing any litter from a vehicle or anywhere in public is illegal. The 'Don't Mess with Alabama' campaign actively enforces and reports violators. Authorities can ask the registered vehicle owner to identify the litterer.
laws.penalty: First offense: $100–$500. Repeat offenses: up to $1,000. Community service may be ordered.
laws.exceptions: Licensed refuse collectors using appropriate equipment

quiz.q: Who can be held responsible for litter thrown from a vehicle in Alabama?
options: The registered vehicle owner can be asked to identify the thrower
quiz.explanation: Alabama can contact the registered vehicle owner to identify who threw litter from the vehicle.

laws.title: Hunting License Requirements
laws.subtitle: AL Code §9-11-44 — Hunting without license
laws.fullDescription: Alabama requires a hunting license for most game. Residents pay lower fees; non-residents pay more. Licenses are required for deer, turkey, small game, and more. Hunting without a license is a criminal offense.
laws.penalty: Hunting without license: $50–$200 fine, potential suspension of hunting privileges.
laws.exceptions: Landowners hunting on their own land with no fee changing hands, youth under 16 on private land with adult

quiz.q: Do landowners need a hunting license to hunt on their own property in Alabama?
options: No, landowners are exempt on their own land
quiz.explanation: Landowners hunting on their own land without selling the game are generally exempt from Alabama's hunting license requirement.

laws.title: Illegal Dumping — Felony Offense
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-7-29(b) — Illegal dumping
laws.fullDescription: Dumping large quantities of waste — including appliances, construction debris, or hazardous materials — at unauthorized sites is a felony in Alabama. This includes disposing of waste on roadsides, in streams, or on others' property.
laws.penalty: Dumping over 500 pounds or hazardous materials: Class C felony, 1–10 years prison. Dumping under 500 lbs: misdemeanor.
laws.exceptions: Licensed waste disposal facilities, permitted construction sites

quiz.q: What is the penalty for dumping hazardous materials illegally in Alabama?
quiz.explanation: Illegal dumping of hazardous materials is a Class C felony in Alabama carrying 1–10 years imprisonment.

laws.title: Homestead Exemption — Property Tax
laws.subtitle: AL Code §40-9-19 — Homestead tax exemption
laws.fullDescription: Alabama offers a homestead exemption that reduces the assessed value of a primary residence for property tax purposes. Standard exemption is $4,000 off assessed value. Residents over 65 or totally disabled may qualify for larger exemptions or full exemption.
laws.penalty: N/A — benefit; misrepresenting eligibility is tax fraud.
laws.exceptions: Non-primary residences, rental properties

quiz.q: Who may qualify for a full property tax exemption on their home in Alabama?
quiz.explanation: Residents over 65 or totally disabled may qualify for a full property tax homestead exemption in Alabama.

laws.title: Landlord Entry Notice — 2 Days Required
laws.subtitle: AL Code §35-9A-303 — Landlord right of entry
laws.fullDescription: Alabama landlords must give at least 2 days (48 hours) advance written notice before entering a rental unit for non-emergency repairs, inspections, or showings. Emergency entry (fire, flood, emergency repairs) is allowed without notice.
laws.penalty: Unauthorized entry: tenant may seek injunctive relief or terminate lease; damages available.
laws.exceptions: Emergencies endangering life or property, tenant has abandoned the premises

quiz.q: How much advance notice must an Alabama landlord give before entering a rental unit?
quiz.explanation: Alabama requires landlords to give at least 48 hours (2 days) advance notice before entering for non-emergency purposes.

laws.title: Open Range Law — Livestock on Roads
laws.subtitle: AL Code §35-9-1 — Livestock and fencing
laws.fullDescription: Alabama has 'open range' areas in some rural counties where livestock owners are NOT required to fence their animals in. In these areas, drivers must watch for livestock on the road and may not have a legal claim if they hit an animal.
laws.penalty: Varies — in open range areas, drivers may bear responsibility for accidents with livestock.
laws.exceptions: Most Alabama counties have moved to closed range; check your county

quiz.q: In Alabama's 'open range' areas, who is responsible for keeping livestock off roads?
options: There is no requirement in open range areas
quiz.explanation: In Alabama open range areas, livestock owners have no legal duty to fence animals in — drivers must watch for animals.

laws.title: Smoking Age — 21
laws.subtitle: AL Code §28-11-14 — Tobacco sales to minors
laws.fullDescription: The minimum age to purchase tobacco products (cigarettes, cigars, smokeless tobacco) and e-cigarettes in Alabama is 21, following federal law. Retailers who sell to those under 21 face significant penalties.
laws.penalty: First offense: $100 fine. Subsequent offenses up to $500. Repeated violations: license suspension.
laws.exceptions: None

quiz.q: What is the minimum age to purchase tobacco in Alabama?
quiz.explanation: Alabama follows the federal Tobacco 21 law — minimum purchase age for tobacco and e-cigarettes is 21.

laws.title: Mandatory Vaccination — Schools
laws.subtitle: AL Dept. of Health vaccine requirements
laws.fullDescription: Alabama requires certain vaccinations for children attending public school — including MMR, Varicella, DTaP, Hep B, Meningococcal, and others based on age. Parents may claim a religious exemption.
laws.penalty: Children not vaccinated (without exemption) may be excluded from school.
laws.exceptions: Medical contraindication with physician letter, religious exemption available

quiz.q: Can Alabama parents exempt their children from school vaccine requirements?
quiz.explanation: Alabama allows religious exemptions from school vaccination requirements, in addition to medical contraindications.

laws.title: Data Breach Notification Law
laws.subtitle: AL Code §8-38-1 — Data Protection Act
laws.fullDescription: Alabama's Data Protection Act requires businesses to implement reasonable security measures for sensitive personal information and to notify affected individuals within 45 days of discovering a data breach.
laws.penalty: Civil penalties up to $500,000 per breach incident for willful violations.
laws.exceptions: If investigation shows breach likely won't cause harm, notification may not be required

quiz.q: Within how many days must Alabama businesses notify customers of a data breach?
quiz.explanation: Alabama's Data Protection Act requires notification within 45 days of discovering a breach affecting sensitive personal information.

laws.title: Cyberstalking — Criminal Offense
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-6-90.1 — Electronic harassment
laws.fullDescription: Using electronic communications to repeatedly harass, threaten, or intimidate another person is cyberstalking in Alabama — a criminal offense. Includes text messages, social media, email, and online posts.
laws.penalty: Class C felony: 1–10 years prison, $15,000 fine.
laws.exceptions: Journalism, lawful law enforcement activity, protected speech

quiz.q: Is cyberstalking a felony in Alabama?
options: Only if the victim is a minor
quiz.explanation: Cyberstalking is a Class C felony in Alabama, punishable by up to 10 years in prison.

laws.title: Fake Mustaches in Church — Historic Law
laws.subtitle: Historical Alabama ordinance — causing laughter prohibited
laws.fullDescription: Alabama reportedly has an old ordinance that prohibits wearing fake mustaches in church if they cause laughter. While largely unenforced and more of a historical curiosity, it reflects early 20th-century community standards laws still on some books.
laws.penalty: Historically: small fine or ejection from premises. Not actively enforced.
laws.exceptions: N/A

quiz.q: What unusual thing is reportedly banned in Alabama churches by an old ordinance?
options: Wearing fake mustaches that cause laughter
quiz.explanation: Alabama reportedly has an old ordinance against wearing fake mustaches in church if they cause laughter — a well-known quirky law.

laws.title: Sunday Work Restrictions — Historical Blue Laws
laws.subtitle: Historical Alabama Code — Sunday commerce limits
laws.fullDescription: Alabama historically had 'blue laws' restricting commerce on Sundays. Most have been repealed or made local options, but some counties still restrict certain commercial activities on Sundays, particularly vehicle sales. Car dealerships in many counties cannot be open on Sundays.
laws.penalty: Car dealers violating Sunday closure: fine and license risk.
laws.exceptions: Varies by county; most restrictions have been modernized

quiz.q: In many Alabama counties, what type of business cannot operate on Sundays?
quiz.explanation: Many Alabama counties still require car dealerships to close on Sundays under remnants of blue laws.

laws.title: Lane Splitting — Prohibited
laws.subtitle: Alabama does not permit lane splitting
laws.fullDescription: Lane splitting (motorcycles riding between lanes of traffic) is not legal in Alabama. Motorcycles must occupy a full lane and may not pass vehicles by traveling between lanes of moving or stopped traffic.
laws.penalty: Traffic violation: fine and points on license.
laws.exceptions: Bicycles and low-speed vehicles have different rules; authorized emergency vehicles

quiz.q: Is lane splitting (riding between traffic lanes) legal for motorcycles in Alabama?
quiz.explanation: Lane splitting is not legal in Alabama; motorcycles must occupy a full lane like other vehicles.

laws.title: Graduated Driver's License — Teen Restrictions
laws.subtitle: AL Code §32-6-7 — GDL program
laws.fullDescription: Alabama's Graduated Driver Licensing (GDL) program restricts teenage drivers. Learner's permit at 15, restricted license at 16 (no driving midnight–6am, one unrelated passenger). Full unrestricted license at 17.
laws.penalty: Violations of GDL restrictions: $100 fine, license suspension.
laws.exceptions: Driving to/from school, work, or family emergency

quiz.q: What is the curfew for 16-year-old drivers under Alabama's GDL program?
quiz.explanation: Alabama's GDL program prohibits 16-year-old drivers from driving between midnight and 6 AM.

laws.title: Public Intoxication — Criminal Offense
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-11-10 — Drunk in public
laws.fullDescription: Being intoxicated in a public place to the degree of being a danger to yourself or others, or engaging in disturbing conduct, is a criminal offense in Alabama.
laws.penalty: Class C misdemeanor: up to 3 months jail and $500 fine.
laws.exceptions: Private property, licensed premises where consumption is permitted

quiz.q: Public intoxication in Alabama is what level of offense?
quiz.explanation: Public intoxication to the point of causing danger is a Class C misdemeanor in Alabama.

laws.title: Waterway Littering — Stream Pollution
laws.subtitle: AL Code §22-22-9 — Water pollution control
laws.fullDescription: Throwing trash, debris, or pollutants into Alabama's rivers, streams, lakes, or coastal waters is illegal. Alabama takes waterway protection seriously given its biodiversity (most freshwater fish species in the US).
laws.penalty: $100–$25,000 per violation depending on severity and type of pollutant.
laws.exceptions: Permitted discharges under NPDES permits, treated stormwater

quiz.q: Why does Alabama take waterway protection especially seriously?
options: It has the most freshwater fish species in the US
quiz.explanation: Alabama has more species of freshwater fish than any other US state, making waterway protection a priority.

laws.title: No Firearms on School Property
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-11-72 — School property gun ban
laws.fullDescription: Bringing a firearm onto any K-12 school property, school bus, or at a school function is a felony in Alabama, regardless of permit status. This is a stricter standard than general carry laws.
laws.penalty: Class C felony: 1–10 years prison.
laws.exceptions: Law enforcement, authorized security personnel, firearms in locked vehicles in school parking lots (debated)

quiz.q: Is carrying a firearm onto school property a felony in Alabama?
options: No, permit holders can carry anywhere
Only if the gun is loaded
quiz.explanation: Bringing a firearm onto K-12 school property is a Class C felony in Alabama even for permit holders.

laws.title: Drinking and Gaming Machines — Prohibited
laws.subtitle: AL Code §28-3A-20 — Restrictions on licensed premises
laws.fullDescription: Alabama prohibits gambling machines (slot machines, video poker, etc.) on premises licensed to sell alcohol. The ABC Board closely regulates what activities can occur on licensed premises.
laws.penalty: License revocation, $1,000–$5,000 fine per violation.
laws.exceptions: Amusement-only games with no cash payout, licensed bingo facilities (separate from alcohol license)

quiz.q: Can Alabama alcohol-licensed venues have slot machines?
options: No, gambling devices are prohibited on alcohol-licensed premises
quiz.explanation: Alabama prohibits gambling machines on premises holding an alcohol license.

laws.title: Resisting Arrest — Criminal Charge
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-10-41 — Obstructing governmental operations
laws.fullDescription: Resisting arrest in Alabama — using physical force or creating a substantial risk of injury to a police officer during an arrest — is a criminal offense. Even verbal obstruction can rise to the level of hindering a law officer.
laws.penalty: Resisting arrest: Class C misdemeanor to Class C felony depending on force used.
laws.exceptions: Unlawful arrest (excessive force by officer) may be a defense in civil proceedings but rarely criminal

quiz.q: Physically resisting arrest in Alabama can rise to what level?
quiz.explanation: Resisting arrest with force can rise to a Class C felony in Alabama depending on the level of resistance.

laws.title: Dangerous Dog Law
laws.subtitle: AL Code §3-6A-1 — Dangerous dog registration
laws.fullDescription: Alabama requires owners of dogs declared dangerous to register them, keep them confined, carry liability insurance of at least $100,000, post warning signs, and sterilize the animal. A second dangerous incident can result in euthanasia.
laws.penalty: Failure to comply: Class A misdemeanor, seizure of dog. If dog causes death: owner faces criminal charges.
laws.exceptions: Police service dogs, dogs acting in defense of their owner from criminal attack

quiz.q: What minimum liability insurance must Alabama owners of dangerous dogs carry?
quiz.explanation: Alabama requires dangerous dog owners to maintain at least $100,000 in liability insurance.

laws.title: Outdoor Burning Restrictions
laws.subtitle: AL Code §9-13-10 — Forest protection burning rules
laws.fullDescription: Outdoor burning in Alabama is regulated seasonally. During red flag conditions (dry, windy weather), the Alabama Forestry Commission may issue burning bans. Burning within 300 feet of a building without permission is restricted. Permits may be required.
laws.penalty: Illegal burning causing fire spread: up to $25,000 fine and potential criminal charges.
laws.exceptions: Controlled burns with proper permits, agricultural burns with notice to forestry commission

quiz.q: How close to a building can you burn outdoors in Alabama without restriction?
quiz.explanation: Outdoor burning within 300 feet of a building in Alabama requires permission and may be restricted under forestry rules.

laws.title: Payday Lending Regulations
laws.subtitle: AL Code §5-18A-1 — Deferred Presentment Services
laws.fullDescription: Alabama regulates payday lenders under the Deferred Presentment Services Act. Maximum loan is $500. Maximum fee is 17.5% of the loan amount. Borrowers cannot have more than $500 in payday loans outstanding at one time. Loan term 10–31 days.
laws.penalty: Unlicensed payday lending: criminal penalties. Violations of fee caps: civil liability to borrower.
laws.exceptions: Banks and credit unions operating under separate lending laws

quiz.q: What is Alabama's maximum payday loan amount?
quiz.explanation: Alabama limits payday loans to $500 maximum with a maximum fee of 17.5% of the borrowed amount.

laws.title: Assault — Degrees and Penalties
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-6-20 — Criminal assault
laws.fullDescription: Alabama assault ranges from 1st degree (intent to cause serious physical injury with a weapon) to 3rd degree (simple assault causing bodily harm or threats). First-degree assault is a Class B felony.
laws.penalty: 1st degree: 2–20 years. 2nd degree: 1–10 years. 3rd degree: up to 1 year.
laws.exceptions: Self-defense (Stand Your Ground), defense of others, defense of property

quiz.q: What is the minimum sentence for 1st degree assault in Alabama?
quiz.explanation: First-degree assault is a Class B felony in Alabama with a minimum 2-year sentence.

laws.title: Railroad Crossing Safety Law
laws.subtitle: AL Code §32-5A-150 — Railroad crossing requirements
laws.fullDescription: Alabama drivers must stop within 15–50 feet of a railroad crossing when gates are down or signals are active. Never stop on the tracks. If a school bus or hazmat vehicle, must always stop and look.
laws.penalty: Running railroad crossing: $100–$500 fine, potential criminal charges if accident results.
laws.exceptions: Emergency vehicles with active lights/siren may proceed carefully

quiz.q: How far from railroad tracks must a driver stop when the signals are active in Alabama?
options: As far as the gate extends
quiz.explanation: Alabama requires drivers to stop 15–50 feet from railroad tracks when signals or gates are active.

laws.title: Abortion Restrictions — Near Total Ban
laws.subtitle: AL Human Life Protection Act — HB 314 (2019)
laws.fullDescription: Alabama enacted one of the most restrictive abortion laws in the US in 2019 (effective following Dobbs decision in 2022). Abortion is banned in nearly all circumstances, including cases of rape and incest. Physicians performing abortions face felony charges. Medical exceptions for serious health risk to mother exist.
laws.penalty: Performing an abortion: Class A felony, 10–99 years in prison for the physician.
laws.exceptions: Documented serious health risk to the mother; ectopic pregnancies

quiz.q: Under Alabama's abortion law, what is the penalty for a physician performing an abortion?
options: Class A felony, up to 99 years prison
quiz.explanation: Alabama's Human Life Protection Act makes performing an abortion a Class A felony for physicians, with up to 99 years in prison.

laws.title: Illegal Gambling Devices — Prohibited
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-12-20 — Gambling offense
laws.fullDescription: Possessing, operating, or allowing on your premises any gambling device (slot machines, electronic gaming machines, etc.) is a criminal offense in Alabama. The state actively prosecutes illegal gaming operations.
laws.penalty: Class A misdemeanor for possession; Class D felony for operating an illegal gambling house.
laws.exceptions: Charitable bingo with license, legitimate amusement games (no cash prizes)

quiz.q: Operating an illegal gambling house in Alabama is what level of offense?
quiz.explanation: Operating an illegal gambling house in Alabama is a Class D felony.

laws.title: Straw Purchase of Firearms — Felony
laws.subtitle: Federal law + AL enforcement — 18 U.S.C. §922(a)
laws.fullDescription: Buying a firearm on behalf of someone else (straw purchase) — particularly for someone prohibited from buying one — is a federal felony enforced in Alabama. ATF and Alabama law enforcement actively prosecute these cases.
laws.penalty: Federal felony: up to 10 years prison and $250,000 fine.
laws.exceptions: Legitimate gifts of firearms between family members in some circumstances

quiz.q: Buying a gun on behalf of a prohibited person (straw purchase) in Alabama is what type of offense?
quiz.explanation: Straw purchases of firearms are federal felonies punishable by up to 10 years in prison.

laws.title: Alligator Hunting License Required
laws.subtitle: AL Code §9-11-267 — Alligator season
laws.fullDescription: Alabama has regulated alligator hunting seasons. A special license and tag are required to hunt alligators. Hunting outside the season or without a tag is illegal. Alligators may not be taken from private water without landowner permission.
laws.penalty: Illegal alligator hunting: $500–$2,000 fine, criminal charges, forfeiture of equipment.
laws.exceptions: Nuisance alligator control by licensed agents, landowner protection of livestock

quiz.q: Does Alabama allow recreational alligator hunting?
options: Yes, with a special license and tag during season
Yes, year-round with a regular hunting license
quiz.explanation: Alabama has a regulated alligator hunting season requiring a special license and harvest tag.

laws.title: Abandoned Property — 3-Year Rule
laws.subtitle: AL Code §35-12-70 — Unclaimed property law
laws.fullDescription: Alabama requires businesses, banks, and other holders to turn over unclaimed property (bank accounts, uncashed checks, insurance proceeds, etc.) to the state after 3 years of inactivity. The state holds the property and owners can claim it through the Unclaimed Property Division.
laws.penalty: Failure to report and remit: civil penalties up to 25% of the value of unreported property.
laws.exceptions: Property actively in use or with demonstrated owner contact

quiz.q: After how many years of inactivity does Alabama require property to be turned over to the state as unclaimed?
quiz.explanation: Alabama's unclaimed property law requires holders to remit dormant property to the state after 3 years of inactivity.

laws.title: Arson — Degrees and Penalties
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-7-41 — Arson in the first degree
laws.fullDescription: Arson in Alabama is classified by the type of property damaged. First-degree arson (inhabited building) is a Class A felony. Second-degree (uninhabited building) is a Class B felony. Third-degree (other property) is a Class C felony.
laws.penalty: 1st degree: 10 years to life. 2nd degree: 2–20 years. 3rd degree: 1–10 years.
laws.exceptions: Controlled burns with permits (not arson), self-defense burning of own property (legal)

quiz.q: Setting fire to an inhabited building in Alabama is what class of felony?
quiz.explanation: Arson of an inhabited building (1st degree arson) is a Class A felony in Alabama carrying 10 years to life.

laws.title: Alcohol in Fitness Centers — Permitted
laws.subtitle: AL ABC Board — Beer/wine retail license for gyms
laws.fullDescription: Alabama passed legislation in 2019 allowing fitness centers and gyms to obtain an Alcohol Beverage License to serve beer and wine to members. This is a relatively new development given Alabama's historically conservative alcohol laws.
laws.penalty: Serving alcohol without proper license: license forfeiture, fines up to $5,000.
laws.exceptions: Must obtain ABC Board approval; limited to beer and wine typically

quiz.q: Can Alabama gyms and fitness centers legally serve alcohol?
options: Yes, since 2019 with proper ABC license
quiz.explanation: A 2019 Alabama law allows gyms to serve beer and wine to members with an ABC Board license.

laws.title: Burglary — Unlawful Entry to Commit Crime
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-7-5 — Burglary degrees
laws.fullDescription: Burglary in Alabama involves unlawfully entering or remaining in a building to commit a crime inside. First-degree burglary (occupied dwelling with weapon or threat) is a Class A felony. Third-degree (unoccupied structure) is a Class C felony.
laws.penalty: 1st degree: 10 years to life. 2nd degree: 2–20 years. 3rd degree: 1–10 years.
laws.exceptions: Lawful entry (maintenance, public buildings open to public)

quiz.q: Breaking into an occupied home with a weapon in Alabama is what class of felony?
quiz.explanation: First-degree burglary of an occupied dwelling with a weapon is a Class A felony in Alabama.

laws.title: Street Racing — Criminal Offense
laws.subtitle: AL Code §32-5A-178 — Illegal drag racing
laws.fullDescription: Participating in or facilitating an illegal street race (drag racing) on a public road in Alabama is a criminal offense. Spectators who block traffic to watch a race can also be charged.
laws.penalty: $200–$500 fine, license suspension, misdemeanor charges. Injury/death: felony charges.
laws.exceptions: Licensed motor sports on private tracks with permits

quiz.q: Can spectators of illegal street races be charged in Alabama?
quiz.explanation: Spectators who block traffic to watch an illegal street race in Alabama can also face criminal charges.

laws.title: Prescription Drug Monitoring Program
laws.subtitle: AL PDMP — Controlled Substance Monitoring Database
laws.fullDescription: Alabama's Prescription Drug Monitoring Program (PDMP) requires pharmacists to report all Schedule II–V controlled substance dispensing to a statewide database. Prescribers must check the database before prescribing opioids and other controlled substances.
laws.penalty: Failure to report: $100–$1,000 per violation. Failure to check database before prescribing: professional license risk.
laws.exceptions: Emergency prescriptions, veterinary use (separate tracking)

quiz.q: What must Alabama prescribers check before prescribing opioids?
quiz.explanation: Alabama prescribers must check the Prescription Drug Monitoring Program (PDMP) database before prescribing opioids and controlled substances.

laws.title: Harassment — Electronic and Otherwise
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-11-8 — Harassment and stalking
laws.fullDescription: Harassing another person through communications, phone calls, or conduct intended to annoy, alarm, or threaten is illegal in Alabama. Repeated following or surveillance is stalking. Electronic harassment using devices or the internet falls under cyberstalking.
laws.penalty: Harassment: Class C misdemeanor. Stalking: Class C felony (up to 10 years).
laws.exceptions: Journalism, legitimate business communication, legal process

quiz.q: Stalking (repeated following/surveillance) in Alabama is what offense?
quiz.explanation: Stalking is a Class C felony in Alabama, while simple harassment is a Class C misdemeanor.

laws.title: Income Tax — Individual and Corporate
laws.subtitle: AL Code §40-18-5 — State income tax
laws.fullDescription: Alabama imposes a state income tax on individuals (2%–5% progressive rate) and corporations (6.5% flat rate). Alabama is one of few states that allows a deduction for federal income taxes paid, reducing the effective state tax burden.
laws.penalty: Failure to file or pay: 10% penalty per month up to 50%, plus interest.
laws.exceptions: Residents below filing threshold, certain nonprofit income

quiz.q: What makes Alabama's income tax system somewhat unique compared to other states?
options: Federal income taxes paid are deductible on Alabama returns
quiz.explanation: Alabama uniquely allows residents to deduct their federal income taxes paid when calculating Alabama state income taxes.

laws.title: Firearms in Vehicles — Legal Rules
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-11-73 — Stored in vehicle
laws.fullDescription: Since constitutional carry passed, Alabamans can transport a loaded handgun in their vehicle without a permit. Long guns (rifles, shotguns) must be unloaded and not concealed in a vehicle unless the owner has a permit. Always check school zones and other restricted areas.
laws.penalty: Improper transport of long gun: misdemeanor. Carry by prohibited person: felony.
laws.exceptions: Law enforcement, licensed dealers in transport, members of military on duty

quiz.q: Since Alabama's 2023 constitutional carry law, can you have a loaded handgun in your car without a permit?
options: Yes, if you're over 21 and can legally own a firearm
quiz.explanation: Alabama's 2023 constitutional carry law allows adults 21+ to transport loaded handguns in vehicles without a permit.

laws.title: Coastal Zone Management — Beach Access
laws.subtitle: AL Code §9-7A — Coastal Area Management
laws.fullDescription: Alabama's Gulf Coast beaches have specific regulations. Public beach access is protected. Driving on the beach is regulated and may require permits in some areas. Disturbing sea turtle nests is a federal and state crime.
laws.penalty: Driving on beach without permit: $100–$500. Disturbing sea turtle nest: up to $50,000 federal fine.
laws.exceptions: Authorized vehicles (emergency, permitted beach services), beach renourishment projects

quiz.q: What federal and state crime carries up to $50,000 in fines in Alabama's coastal area?
quiz.explanation: Disturbing sea turtle nests in Alabama's coastal area can result in up to $50,000 in federal fines under the Endangered Species Act.

laws.title: Hate Crimes — Enhanced Penalties
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-5-13 — Hate crime sentence enhancement
laws.fullDescription: Alabama's Hate Crime statute enhances sentences when crimes are committed because of the victim's race, religion, national origin, color, sex, disability, sexual orientation, or gender identity. Enhanced penalties add time to existing charges.
laws.penalty: Sentence enhancement: additional 1–5 years on top of base sentence, depending on the underlying crime.
laws.exceptions: Normal criminal penalties without enhancement apply when no bias motivation proven

quiz.q: Alabama hate crime law enhances sentences based on what factors?
options: Race, religion, national origin, sex, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity
quiz.explanation: Alabama's hate crime enhancement applies to crimes motivated by the victim's race, religion, national origin, sex, disability, sexual orientation, or gender identity.

laws.title: Emergency Vehicle Right of Way
laws.subtitle: AL Code §32-5A-58 — Yielding to emergency vehicles
laws.fullDescription: Alabama drivers must immediately pull to the right edge of the road and stop when an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches, regardless of direction of travel. Remain stopped until the emergency vehicle passes.
laws.penalty: Failure to yield: $200–$500 fine, 4 points on license.
laws.exceptions: Intersection where stopping creates more danger — slow and proceed carefully

quiz.q: In Alabama, which direction must you pull over when an emergency vehicle approaches?
options: Only if going the same direction
quiz.explanation: Alabama requires pulling to the right edge of the road and stopping for all approaching emergency vehicles.

laws.title: Adverse Possession — 10-Year Rule
laws.subtitle: AL Code §6-5-200 — Adverse possession statute
laws.fullDescription: In Alabama, a person who openly, continuously, and exclusively occupies another's land for 10 years under a claim of right may be able to gain legal title through adverse possession. The possession must be hostile, actual, open, notorious, exclusive, and continuous.
laws.penalty: N/A — legal doctrine; original owner must file suit within the statutory period to reclaim.
laws.exceptions: Government-owned land, land under active management by owner

quiz.q: How long must a person continuously occupy land in Alabama to potentially claim it through adverse possession?
quiz.explanation: Alabama requires 10 years of continuous, open, exclusive, and hostile possession to support an adverse possession claim.

laws.title: Identity Theft — Felony
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-8-190 — Identity theft act
laws.fullDescription: Using another person's identifying information (Social Security number, account numbers, etc.) without consent to obtain money, credit, or other benefits is identity theft — a felony in Alabama.
laws.penalty: Class C felony: 1–10 years prison. Enhanced to Class B felony if victim is over 60 or under 19, or if multiple victims.
laws.exceptions: Authorized use of another's information (legal guardianship, with consent)

quiz.q: Identity theft targeting a senior over 60 in Alabama is elevated to what class of felony?
quiz.explanation: Alabama elevates identity theft to a Class B felony when the victim is over 60 or under 19.

laws.title: Home Distilling — Illegal
laws.subtitle: AL Code §28-9-1 — Distillation of alcohol
laws.fullDescription: Manufacturing distilled spirits (moonshine) at home without a license is illegal in Alabama. While homebrewing beer and winemaking (under 200 gallons/year for personal use) is legal, home distillation of spirits remains prohibited.
laws.penalty: Unlicensed distillation: misdemeanor to felony depending on quantity. Federal violations may also apply.
laws.exceptions: Licensed commercial distilleries, scientific/industrial permits

quiz.q: Is home distillation of spirits (moonshine) legal in Alabama?
quiz.explanation: Home distillation of spirits is illegal in Alabama; unlike beer and wine homebrewing, no personal-use exception exists for spirits.

laws.title: Mailbox Tampering — Federal Crime
laws.subtitle: 18 U.S.C. §1705 — Destruction of mail receptacles
laws.fullDescription: Tampering with, damaging, or destroying a mailbox — or stealing mail — is a federal crime enforced throughout Alabama. Even hitting a mailbox with a baseball bat ('mailbox baseball') is a federal offense, not just a prank.
laws.penalty: Federal felony: up to 3 years prison and substantial fines. Mail theft carries up to 5 years.
laws.exceptions: Lawful mail carriers, authorized postal work

quiz.q: Destroying a mailbox in Alabama is what type of offense?
quiz.explanation: Mailbox destruction is a federal crime under 18 U.S.C. §1705, with up to 3 years imprisonment.

laws.title: Invasive Species Introduction — Prohibited
laws.subtitle: AL Code §9-2-7 — Wildlife importation
laws.fullDescription: Intentionally introducing invasive species (plants, animals, fish) into Alabama's waterways or ecosystems is illegal. Releasing aquatic bait fish, plants, or other species into public waters without authorization is prohibited.
laws.penalty: $500–$5,000 fine, possible criminal charges for intentional violations.
laws.exceptions: Authorized stocking by ADCNR, aquaculture operations with permits

quiz.q: Is it legal to release aquarium fish into Alabama public waterways?
options: Yes, if fish are native species
No, releasing bait or aquarium fish is prohibited
quiz.explanation: Releasing fish, plants, or other species into Alabama public waters without authorization is prohibited to prevent invasive species spread.

laws.title: BUI — Boating Under the Influence
laws.subtitle: AL Code §33-5-25 — Boating while intoxicated
laws.fullDescription: Operating a motorboat, sailboat, or other watercraft in Alabama with a BAC of 0.08% or higher is Boating Under the Influence (BUI). Same 0.08% standard as driving a car. Applies to all Alabama waterways.
laws.penalty: 1st offense BUI: up to 1 year jail, $600–$2,100 fine, 90-day suspension of boating privileges.
laws.exceptions: Non-motorized canoes/kayaks (no engine) — but public intoxication still applies

quiz.q: What is Alabama's BAC limit for operating a motorboat?
quiz.explanation: Alabama's BUI law applies the same 0.08% BAC limit to motorboat operators as car drivers.

laws.title: Bribery of Public Officials — Felony
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-10-60 — Bribery
laws.fullDescription: Offering, giving, receiving, or soliciting something of value to influence an official act by a public servant, judge, juror, or witness is bribery — a Class B felony in Alabama.
laws.penalty: Class B felony: 2–20 years prison, permanent disqualification from public office.
laws.exceptions: Lawful campaign contributions, per diem and legitimate expense reimbursements

quiz.q: Bribing a public official in Alabama is what class of felony?
quiz.explanation: Bribery of a public official is a Class B felony in Alabama, carrying 2–20 years and permanent disqualification from public office.

laws.title: U-Turn Restrictions
laws.subtitle: AL Code §32-5A-90 — Prohibited turns
laws.fullDescription: U-turns in Alabama are prohibited in business districts unless made from the far left lane. Also prohibited where signs prohibit them, near hills or curves where you can't be seen, and at intersections where they create a traffic hazard.
laws.penalty: $100 fine, 2 points on license.
laws.exceptions: Emergency vehicles, authorized vehicles in the performance of duty

quiz.q: Where are U-turns prohibited in Alabama business districts?
options: Only if not from the far left lane
Business districts have no U-turn restrictions
quiz.explanation: In Alabama business districts, U-turns are only permitted when made from the far left lane; otherwise they are prohibited.

laws.title: Money Laundering — State and Federal
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-9-6.1 — Money laundering
laws.fullDescription: Conducting financial transactions knowing the money is derived from criminal activity, in order to conceal its source or evade taxes, is money laundering — a felony in Alabama and federally.
laws.penalty: Class B felony: 2–20 years. Federal money laundering: up to 20 years.
laws.exceptions: Banks reporting suspicious activity (safe harbor), lawful transactions

quiz.q: Money laundering in Alabama is at minimum what class of felony?
quiz.explanation: Money laundering is a Class B felony in Alabama, carrying 2–20 years, in addition to potential federal charges.

laws.title: Tenant Security Deposit — Rules
laws.subtitle: AL Code §35-9A-201 — Security deposit limits
laws.fullDescription: Alabama law does not cap the amount of security deposit a landlord can charge. However, landlords must return the deposit within 35 days of lease termination (or 60 days if the tenant gives written notice). Itemized deductions must be provided.
laws.penalty: Wrongful withholding: tenant may recover up to 2x the deposit plus attorney fees.
laws.exceptions: Deposits held for damages or unpaid rent (with itemization required)

quiz.q: Within how many days must an Alabama landlord return a security deposit after lease ends?
quiz.explanation: Alabama landlords have 35 days to return security deposits (or 60 days with tenant's written notice), along with an itemized list of deductions.

laws.title: Human Trafficking — Severe Penalties
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-6-152 — Human trafficking
laws.fullDescription: Human trafficking — both labor trafficking and sex trafficking — is a Class A felony in Alabama. The state has enacted comprehensive anti-trafficking laws including enhanced penalties when victims are children.
laws.penalty: Class A felony: 10 years to life. Trafficking of children: mandatory life without parole.
laws.exceptions: None — no consent of victim can be used as a defense

quiz.q: What is the sentence for trafficking a child in Alabama?
quiz.explanation: Human trafficking of a child in Alabama carries a mandatory sentence of life without the possibility of parole.

laws.title: Sexting — Minors
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-6-240 — Electronic solicitation of a child
laws.fullDescription: Sending, receiving, or possessing sexually explicit images of minors via any electronic device is illegal in Alabama. This includes 'selfies' sent between teens — both sender and receiver can face charges. Alabama treats this as a serious offense rather than just a juvenile matter.
laws.penalty: Producing/possessing child sexual imagery: Class B felony. Sexting between teens: Class A misdemeanor for first offense under teen sexting provision.
laws.exceptions: Law enforcement investigations, medical documentation

quiz.q: In Alabama, can a teenager sending a racy self-image to another teen face criminal charges?
options: Yes, under a teen sexting provision
Only if sent to an adult
quiz.explanation: Alabama has a teen sexting provision — minors who send explicit images to peers can face Class A misdemeanor charges.

laws.title: Cottage Food Law
laws.subtitle: AL Code §2-20-2 — Home food production
laws.fullDescription: Alabama's Cottage Food Law allows home-based food production businesses selling non-potentially-hazardous foods (baked goods, jams, candy) directly to consumers. Annual sales limit of $20,000. Products must be labeled and cannot be sold in retail stores.
laws.penalty: Selling cottage food in stores or exceeding sales limit: violation of food safety laws, fines.
laws.exceptions: Only non-potentially-hazardous foods; no meat, dairy, or refrigerated items

quiz.q: What is Alabama's annual sales limit for cottage food businesses?
quiz.explanation: Alabama's Cottage Food Law allows home food businesses to sell up to $20,000 in products annually directly to consumers.

laws.title: Disorderly Conduct
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-11-7 — Disorderly conduct
laws.fullDescription: Engaging in fighting, threatening behavior, creating hazardous conditions, or making unreasonable noise in public constitutes disorderly conduct in Alabama. Also includes blocking traffic or pedestrian flow.
laws.penalty: Class C misdemeanor: up to 3 months jail and $500 fine.
laws.exceptions: Lawful assembly, public protest with permits, expressive speech protected by First Amendment

quiz.q: Disorderly conduct in Alabama is classified as what level of offense?
quiz.explanation: Disorderly conduct in Alabama is a Class C misdemeanor, punishable by up to 3 months jail and a $500 fine.

laws.title: Pesticide Application — Licensing Required
laws.subtitle: AL Code §2-27-6 — Pesticide registration and licensing
laws.fullDescription: Applying pesticides (other than consumer-grade products for personal use) commercially in Alabama requires a Certified Applicator license from the Alabama Department of Agriculture. Unlicensed commercial pesticide application is illegal.
laws.penalty: Operating without license: $500–$5,000 fine, seizure of equipment.
laws.exceptions: Homeowners applying to their own property, unlicensed applicators working under direct supervision of licensed applicator

quiz.q: Who must be licensed to apply pesticides commercially in Alabama?
quiz.explanation: All commercial pesticide applicators in Alabama must hold a Certified Applicator license from the Department of Agriculture.

laws.title: Bicycle Laws — Rights and Responsibilities
laws.subtitle: AL Code §32-5A-260 — Bicycle rules of the road
laws.fullDescription: In Alabama, bicycles are vehicles and cyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicle drivers on public roads. Must ride as far right as practicable, use hand signals, obey all traffic signals. Cyclists under 16 must wear helmets.
laws.penalty: Traffic violations same as motor vehicles: $50–$200 fines. No helmet for under-16: $25 fine.
laws.exceptions: Bike lanes, multi-use paths (separate rules), bicycling on sidewalk may be allowed in some areas

quiz.q: Are helmets legally required for cyclists of all ages in Alabama?
quiz.explanation: Alabama requires helmets for cyclists under 16; riders 16 and older are not legally required to wear a helmet.

laws.title: Food Safety — Restaurant Inspections
laws.subtitle: AL Code §22-20-5 — Food service establishments
laws.fullDescription: Alabama food service establishments must pass regular unannounced inspections by the Alabama Department of Public Health. Scores are graded A–F. Establishments with failing scores can be closed immediately. Health inspection results are public record.
laws.penalty: Closure for critical violations, fines up to $5,000 per day for operating while closed.
laws.exceptions: Temporary food booths at events (have lighter but still required inspections)

quiz.q: Can Alabama health inspectors close a restaurant that fails inspection?
options: Yes, immediate closure is possible for critical violations
quiz.explanation: Alabama health inspectors can immediately close a food establishment with critical violations posing immediate health risks.

laws.title: Child Abuse — Mandatory Reporting
laws.subtitle: AL Code §26-14-3 — Mandatory reporters
laws.fullDescription: Alabama law mandates that certain professionals (teachers, doctors, nurses, social workers, law enforcement, and others) report known or suspected child abuse or neglect to the Department of Human Resources or law enforcement. Failure to report is a criminal offense.
laws.penalty: Failure to report (mandatory reporter): Class A misdemeanor. False report: Class B misdemeanor.
laws.exceptions: Attorney-client privilege in limited circumstances; the privilege does not apply to mandatory reporters in most cases

quiz.q: In Alabama, failing to report suspected child abuse as a mandatory reporter is what offense?
quiz.explanation: Mandatory reporters in Alabama who fail to report suspected child abuse face Class A misdemeanor charges.

laws.title: Spam Email — CAN-SPAM Act Enforcement
laws.subtitle: Federal CAN-SPAM Act — enforced in Alabama
laws.fullDescription: Sending bulk unsolicited commercial emails (spam) in violation of the federal CAN-SPAM Act is illegal in Alabama, where federal law is the primary enforcement mechanism. Must include opt-out, physical address, and honest subject lines.
laws.penalty: Civil penalties up to $51,744 per violation (per email for large campaigns). Criminal penalties for intentional violations.
laws.exceptions: Transactional emails, emails to existing customers, personal communications

quiz.q: Under CAN-SPAM Act, what must every commercial email include?
options: A working opt-out mechanism and physical address
quiz.explanation: The CAN-SPAM Act requires commercial emails to include a working opt-out mechanism and a valid physical postal address.

laws.title: Animal Cruelty — Felony
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-11-14.1 — Aggravated cruelty to animals
laws.fullDescription: Intentionally torturing, mutilating, or killing an animal in Alabama is aggravated animal cruelty — a Class C felony. Simple neglect or mistreatment is a misdemeanor. Alabama also has specific protections for police and military dogs.
laws.penalty: Aggravated cruelty: Class C felony, 1–10 years. Simple cruelty: Class A misdemeanor. Harming a police dog: Class C felony.
laws.exceptions: Livestock management, hunting, pest control, veterinary treatment

quiz.q: Intentionally torturing an animal in Alabama is what type of offense?
quiz.explanation: Intentional torture or mutilation of an animal (aggravated cruelty) is a Class C felony in Alabama.

laws.title: Grand Theft — Felony Threshold $500
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-8-3 — Theft by value
laws.fullDescription: In Alabama, theft of property valued at $500 or more is felony theft. Theft under $500 is a misdemeanor. The value thresholds are: under $500 = Class A misdemeanor; $500–$2,500 = Class D felony; over $2,500 = Class C or higher felony.
laws.penalty: Under $500: up to 1 year jail. $500–$2,500: 1–5 years. Over $2,500: 1–10 years. Major theft: 2–20 years.
laws.exceptions: Color of right (belief you own the property), returning property may mitigate but not eliminate charges

quiz.q: At what dollar amount does theft become a felony in Alabama?
quiz.explanation: Theft of $500 or more is a felony in Alabama (Class D felony); under $500 is a misdemeanor.

laws.title: Pregnancy Discrimination — Illegal
laws.subtitle: Federal PWFA + AL law — workplace protections
laws.fullDescription: Discriminating against employees or job applicants because of pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions is illegal in Alabama under federal law (Pregnancy Discrimination Act) and the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act. Employers must provide reasonable accommodations.
laws.penalty: Civil liability: back pay, compensatory and punitive damages, attorney fees.
laws.exceptions: Undue hardship to employer (very narrow exception for accommodations)

quiz.q: Can an Alabama employer legally fire someone for being pregnant?
options: Only if they can't perform their duties
quiz.explanation: Pregnancy discrimination is illegal in Alabama (and all US states) under the federal Pregnancy Discrimination Act.

laws.title: Explosive Devices — Felony Possession
laws.subtitle: AL Code §13A-11-260 — Explosive devices
laws.fullDescription: Manufacturing, possessing, or using explosive or incendiary devices (pipe bombs, Molotov cocktails, etc.) without proper authorization is a serious felony in Alabama. This includes components assembled for use as an explosive device.
laws.penalty: Possession of explosive device: Class B felony (2–20 years). Use causing injury: Class A felony (10 years to life).
laws.exceptions: Licensed mining and demolition companies, military, authorized law enforcement explosives

quiz.q: Possessing an improvised explosive device in Alabama is what class of felony?
quiz.explanation: Unlawful possession of an explosive device is a Class B felony in Alabama, with 2–20 years imprisonment.

laws.title: Bald Eagle Protection — Federal Law
laws.subtitle: Bald and Golden Eagle Protection Act — enforced in Alabama
laws.fullDescription: It is illegal in Alabama (and all US states) to harm, kill, possess, or disturb bald or golden eagles, their nests, or eggs. Even possessing a bald eagle feather requires federal authorization. The eagle is the national symbol and receives maximum protection.
laws.penalty: First offense: up to $100,000 fine and 1 year prison. Second offense: up to $200,000 and 2 years.
laws.exceptions: Native Americans with permits for religious/cultural use, authorized scientific research
laws.sourceLabel: Bald and Golden Eagle Protection Act

quiz.q: Is it legal to pick up a bald eagle feather found on the ground in Alabama?
options: Yes, if the bird wasn't harmed
Yes, if it's on your property
quiz.explanation: Possessing any bald eagle part, including feathers found on the ground, requires federal authorization under the Bald and Golden Eagle Protection Act.
